issues.legal_issue: Interest under the land acquisition statute is unavailable for a period of possession that precedes publication of the acquisition notification, and a court cannot award interest beyond the statute’s prescribed rate and period.
material_facts: Possession of the land was taken for a public purpose before acquisition proceedings were initiated under the land acquisition statute.
The owners later received compensation following acquisition proceedings initiated by publication of a notification under the statute.
In execution of the decree, the court directed payment of interest at 18% per annum from the date possession was first taken, and the High Court upheld that direction.
issues.conclusion: The owners could not receive statutory interest for the period before publication of the acquisition notification, and the court could not award interest at a rate or for a period beyond that authorized by the statute. The owners were entitled to interest on enhanced compensation at 9% from 16 October 1984; the direction for 18% interest from the date of initial possession was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is a self-contained code governing the State’s liability to pay interest and the owner’s entitlement to it. Sections 4(1), 17, 28 and 34 govern the statutory acquisition process and interest; section 48(2) provides a remedy for damages when acquisition proceedings are withdrawn. Publication of the section 4(1) notification is a condition precedent to possession being treated as possession taken under the Act. Courts cannot use common-law principles of justice, equity and good conscience to award interest contrary to the statute. Vallabhdas Naranji v. Development Officer, Bandra did not decide entitlement to interest for possession predating the notification. Revenue Divisional Officer, Trichinopoly v. Venkatarama Ayyar involved possession connected to the exercise of statutory urgency powers, and State of Punjab v. Raminder Kaur concerned possession taken pursuant to an earlier section 4(1) notification; those decisions were consistent with, rather than contrary to, the statutory scheme.

rule.if: appeal_from_execution_order and possession_taken_before_acquisition_notification and later_acquisition_proceedings_under_statute and statute_prescribes_interest_entitlement and lower_court_awarded_interest_for_pre_notification_period_or_beyond_statutory_rate

predicates.appeal_from_execution_order: The matter is an appeal concerning an order made in execution of a decree.
predicates.possession_taken_before_acquisition_noti: The acquiring authority took possession before publication of the notification that initiated acquisition under the statute.
predicates.later_acquisition_proceedings_under_stat: Acquisition proceedings under the statute were initiated after possession had been taken.
predicates.statute_prescribes_interest_entitlement: The applicable statute specifies when interest is payable and the rate or manner of its payment.
predicates.lower_court_awarded_interest_for_pre_not: The lower court directed interest for a period before the acquisition notification or at a rate exceeding the statutory entitlement.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an execution order involves possession taken before statutory acquisition proceedings and the statute governs interest, the interest outcome is confined to the entitlement the statute provides.
